title: Modular response anchoring — sketch
body:
Goal: quick brain-dump for a lightweight feature set that lets us compose and anchor multiple small response modules (mini-responses) into a single coherent assistant reply. Aim: reduce token cost for common microtasks, enable partial fallbacks and per-module QoS, and make rollout low-risk.

Context / Why:
- Lots of product teams want shorter, structured responses for microtasks (summarize, form-fill, short answer, code-snippets) but also want the ability to escalate to fuller responses when needed.
- Current model-level toggles are coarse (full / economy). We could instead compose a final output from small, specialized response modules that can be cached, re-used, or downgraded independently.
- This ties into session-level budgeting, interaction-economics features, and the console's cost/latency telemetry.

Non-goals:
- Not a full multi-model routing system (for now stick to single model with modular prompts / prompt templates)
- Not an end-user UI: first iteration is API + SDK primitives + a simple console flag.

Success metrics (how we know it's useful):
- Mean tokens per successful microtask down 20% for targeted flows within 90 days.
- Error/fallback rate for economy flows <= 4% (where fallback = escalate to full response)
- Adoption: 3 internal teams trialing within first month; at least one external pilot by month 2.

User personas / user stories (rough):
- As an in-product assistant developer, I want to declare a set of "response modules" (summary, quick-action list, citation block) so that I can mix them into a single reply and charge each module to different QoS buckets.
- As an SRE, I want each module to be independently cacheable so we can reuse heavy computations (e.g., retrieval results) across sessions.
- As a product owner, I want an easy fallback policy: if module A fails or runs long, return the rest and mark A as deferred.
- As a customer, I want consistent token-based billing reporting that shows per-module token breakdowns.

Proposed API sketch (POST /responses/composite)
- body: {
    "modules": [
      {"id":"summary","template_id":"tmpl-12","max_tokens":80,"priority":10},
      {"id":"actions","template_id":"tmpl-08","max_tokens":40,"priority":20, "cache_key": "r:${doc_id}:actions"},
      {"id":"cite","template_id":"tmpl-ref","max_tokens":30,"priority":50}
    ],
    "fallback_policy": "sequential|parallel|best-effort",
    "session_id": "s_...",
    "timeout_ms": 800
  }

Notes on behavior:
- Module execution modes: parallel (fire all, merge), sequential (ordered), conditional (module B only if A triggered). For initial MVP: parallel and sequential.
- Merging logic: simple concatenation with stable boundary markers by default. Hook for structured merging (JSON output) if modules have structured templates.
- Per-module caching: allow TTL, key templates (supports KV cache / prefix caching). Cache hits avoid model calls entirely for that module.
- Per-module QoS: max_tokens, max_latency, priority (used to trim or drop modules under load). Priority small -> high priority or vice versa? Decide: lower number = higher priority.
- Fallbacks: if module fails/timeouts, attach diagnostic marker, return remaining modules. Optionally kickoff async regeneration.

Telemetry / Observability
- Expose per-module token counts, latency, model variant used, cache hit/miss, fallback reason.
- Console: show per-route stacked token cost breakdown (we already have some of this in Console but need module-level UI slice).
- Alerts: sudden spike in module failure rate > X% -> auto-rollout fallback to serial mode.

Rollout and safety
- Start internal: SDK flag for composite responses, no billing exposure.
- Add audit-logs for each module output; tag sensitive modules for redaction checks.
- Canary: 1% external, monitor token delta and failure rate.

Experiment ideas
- Module-level quantization profiles: run small modules on quantized variants to save tokens + compute.
- Heuristic trimming: for low priority modules, run with strict length cap and aggressive nucleus sampling to reduce compute.
- Prefetching modules in background on predicted user intent (e.g., if user clicks certain UI element), store in session cache.

Open design questions / TODOs
- Module spec: what templating language? JSON templates? Must support retrieval injection and tool outputs.
- Authorization: per-module secrets? Probably not. But need to surface which modules can access retrievals/third-party tools.
- Billing model: do we show composite as single bill line with breakdown, or separate billed items per module call? Backend likely records per-module tokens for reporting; billing can be aggregate for now.
- SDK ergonomics: should there be a helper to declare modules and a composer function? Example: composer.addModule("summary", tpl).compose() -> simplifies adoption.
- Edge-case: if all modules fail, what's the user-facing response? Empty with error marker? Provide graceful degraded generic sentence.

Implementation scaffolding (short-term plan)
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): prototype API handler that accepts modules, executes templates sequentially against current model, merges outputs. No caching, minimal telemetry.
- Phase 1 (4–6 weeks): add parallel execution, per-module timeouts, token accounting, and console telemetry slice.
- Phase 2 (6–10 weeks): implement per-module caching, priority-based dropping, and partial async regeneration; start internal pilots.

Notes to self / reminders
- Tie in with session crediting work (Sam O.). Discuss TTL semantics with infra team (Harper). Add a small experiment to compare token savings vs quality drop.
- Checkout PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-orch/pull/642 for template engine tweaks.
- Slack thread: #feature-ideas 2024-09-12 has user requests for "short actionable answers" — pull top 5 examples.

Rough acceptance criteria for Phase 1
- API accepts composite payloads, executes modules, and returns merged response with per-module metadata.
- Console shows per-module token breakdown for requests in trial orgs.
- SDK example in repo /examples/composite-basic demonstrating simple composition (1 summary + 1 actions).

Potential risks
- UX fragmentation (too many module types -> confusing). Mitigate with curated starter module set and templates.
- Increased complexity in billing/quotas. Keep billing stable initially, only reporting visible.

If this lands well, longer-term followups:
- Cross-session module stitching (stitch cached modules into new sessions safely).
- Module marketplace for teams to share templates (internal first).
- Multi-model module routing: cheap models for small modules vs big model for heavy ones.

Random brainlets / snippets:
- "deferred module" marker: {"id":"actions","status":"deferred","reason":"timeout"}
- Consider making module IDs semantic (e.g., summary.v2) to handle rollouts.
